title: Hull-only positions mark structural boundaries rather than relation participants
summary: GDT701 separates two visually intervening hull-only positions from genuine edge nodes. A speculative semantic/functional hypothesis is that hull-only tokens delimit relation scope without entering participant identity, unlike a true edge node.

design.mechanism: hull-only boundary marker versus participant node
design.unit: visually intervening position inside an admitted relation hull but excluded from its edge-node set
design.contrast: boundary scope marker versus semantic participant/result node
design.prediction: Across held relation hulls, hull-only positions should alter scope or closure while never supplying an incoming/outgoing participant; true nodes should recur in edge incidence and participant transitions.
design.countermodel: The exclusion may be an analyst capacity rule, while the intervening token is an omitted participant that happens to lack a current edge.
design.falsifier: A source-observed hull-only position independently receives an edge incidence or participant continuity, or removing it leaves scope and closure unchanged across all held hulls.
design.principal_risk: The hull/node distinction is partly protocol-defined and has no independent lexical meaning binding.
design.related: Near GDT701 and GDT702, but targets the semantic status of explicitly excluded hull positions rather than adding relation edges or result labels.

source_evidence.quote:
The graph has 23 unique edge nodes and 25 edge incidences. Only
`f80v.35#3` and `f86v6.25#4` are genuine shared nodes. Two visually intervening
positions are not nodes:

- `f86v5.24#2 aiin` is an unbound quantity register inside the C010 hull;
- `f26r.2#5 chedy` is an exact state checkpoint inside the C011 hull.

The free `dy` at `f26r.2#7` is retained only to close the rendered clause; it
lies outside C011's #4--#6 hull.
